subject: Operations
title: The Toyota Production System
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The Toyota Production System.

hook.text: After WWII, Toyota was nearly bankrupt. They couldn't afford waste. That constraint became a superpower.

buildup.text: Taiichi Ohno built a system around two pillars: just-in-time production and jidoka—automation with a human touch.

discovery.text: Instead of pushing products through, Toyota pulled—making only what customers actually ordered.

twist.text: Western rivals had bigger budgets but more waste. Toyota's lean system produced more with less.

climax.text: TPS became the foundation of Lean, Six Sigma, and every modern operations improvement framework.

punchline.text: Poverty forced efficiency. Efficiency built an empire.

quiz.question: What are the two pillars of the Toyota Production System?
